title: Sense Trend Sensors Incorrect 'last_reset' Value
body:
I was able to use `sensor.daily_production` and `sensor.daily_usage` as inputs to two template sensors for "grid consumption" and "return to grid" (max of 0 and the relevant difference). This worked fine(*) during the day.

But there's another issue: for me the daily reset occurred at 12:02:32 am, not 12:00:00, despite what the "last_reset" property claims. So the day started out with large negative daily production and usage. I'm not sure if this is due to polling schedule, daily reset schedule at Sense, or something else.

(*) -- worked fine until Sense had an unrelated outage yesterday due to an expired SSL cert

_Originally posted by @dlarrick in https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/53965#issuecomment-894794338_

comments.author: participant11
comments.body:
I too have the problem (2016.12). I also created my own energy sensor using Riemann integration from the sense provided power meter values. For me, through the sense integration, energy (kWh) values seem to be obtained/updated about once per hour, and frequently not until 2 minutes after the hour, whereas power values (W) seem to be updated every 2 minutes. This is possibly the difference between the trend api and the css based real time feed.

The problem with the hourly updates is that, as noted, they come well after the change of the hour. Properly setting last reset can resolve a part of the problem, but it will cause data to be missed because, after all, the value that would have existed at the hour is never seen, yet the value has been reset to 0. So while this may solve the negative spike problem, it will cause the last hour of the day readings to be missed.

The integration of power approach causes at most 2 minutes to be missed, so in that sense is much better. For me that typically amounts to about 0.01-0.02 kWh being missed. However, the Riemann integral introduces its own error. At 2 minute intervals there are 30 samples per hour. For me typical usage is about 1 kWh per hour, so the integration error upper bound is 1/30. Over a day, and in worst case, that can add up to an error of 24/30 = 0.6 kWh which is somewhat consistent with what I see compared to utility meter reports. It seems @participant5 is seeing about the same.

If, somehow, the sampling frequency, at least of the power figures, can be increased we could do better. I don't know enough about the sense api to see what the practical limit here is.

Separately it seems it would be a good idea for the integration to automatically produce these integral sensors for production and consumption, but in general for any current device on the list because the user is almost always interested in energy consumption, not in power usage.

comments.author: participant11
comments.body:
I am currently running with integrated sensors. I have net_power and then split template sensors for power_to_grid and power_from_grid, each clipped against 0 with positive values. Each of these three is then integrated. My production number is typically spot on compared with sense, but for that I am currently using the annual_energy directly (this will cause a spike problem once a year on Jan 1 due to results rolling over about 2 minutes after the hour).

Riemann integration inherently has errors, varying by the nature of the signal, and the chosen integration method. What seems to make matters worse is that when a sensor remains unchanged for a while (e.g. my power_from_grid is 0 most of the sunny daylight hours), Riemann only sees the start and end value of that long interval. This effectively reduces the number of sample taken and increases the computational error.

I have observed that my basic sensor updates every 2 minutes with the current sense integration. That also causes any signal changes within that period to be "lost" or at least miscalculated compared to the actual sense data. When data remains identical between updates, it seems that either the sense integration or the homeassistent features causes nothing to be stored through the recorder. This is what causes the long intervals. What is really needed here is something akin to the force_update option that exists for MQTT sensors.

Separately, I believe that sense can actually provide the "integrated" values themselves. I am working to confirm this, but if true, it would be much better to use those.

comments.author: participant11
comments.body:
I am currently running version 2021.12.10 of Home Assistant and the corresponding Sense integration. I use the following sensors for the energy panel:
* Energy Consumed From Grid, with an associated cost tracking sensor.utility_energy_price
* Energy Sent To Grid, with an associated cost tracking sensor.utility_energy_price
* Solar Energy Produced, with forecast production

The first two sensors do not come from the sense integration. It does make energy sensors available, but they are either per hour, day, week etc. They tend to update only once an hour and roll over about 2 minutes after the hour (for me). That alone causes problems with "strange" accounting in the bar graph:
*  The sense integration looks at the sensor precisely on the hour, but when using sense kWh numbers they don't get updated until about 00:02.
* So at 00:00 the amount is still close to the total of the previous day
* At 00:02 it appears reset to 0, but that is not seen until the next inspection at 01:02
* That's why everything is off by an hour
* I am currently researching if we can do better with the sense api, but have no conclusions yet

That is why I use these two alternate sensors. They are defined as follows in sensors.yaml and seem to "do the trick":
```
- sensor:
  platform: integration
  name: energy_from_grid
  source: sensor.power_from_grid
  method: left
  round: 5
  unit_prefix: k
  unit_time: h

- sensor:
  platform: integration
  name: energy_to_grid
  source: sensor.power_to_grid
  method: left
  round: 5
  unit_prefix: k
  unit_time: h

- sensor:
  platform: integration
  name: net_energy_from_grid
  source: sensor.net_power_from_grid
  round: 8
  unit_prefix: k
  unit_time: h
```

These in turn rely on (templates.yaml):
```
# Sensor that returns instantaneous power (W) taken from grid (>= 0), or put to grid (< 0)
- sensor:
  name: Net Power From Grid
  unique_id: net_power_from_grid
  device_class: power
  unit_of_measurement: W
    # Test both sensors exist
  availability: >-
    {{ true if states.sensor.energy_production and states.sensor.energy_usage }}
  state: >-
    {{ states('sensor.energy_usage') | float(0) - states('sensor.energy_production') | float(0) }}

# Sensor that returns instantaneous power (W) taken from grid (>= 0)
- sensor:
  name: Power From Grid
  unique_id: power_from_grid
  device_class: power
  unit_of_measurement: W
  availability: >-
    {{ true if states.sensor.net_power_from_grid }}
  state: >-
    {{ max(states('sensor.net_power_from_grid') | float(0), 0) }}

# Sensor that returns instantaneous power (W) put to grid (>= 0), or 0 if not putting any
- sensor:
  name: Power To Grid
  unique_id: power_to_grid
  device_class: power
  unit_of_measurement: W
  availability: >-
    {{ true if states.sensor.net_power_from_grid }}
  state: >-
    {{ max(-(states('sensor.net_power_from_grid') | float(0)), 0) }}
```

With this approach my solar production is dead on every day, and my to_grid and from_grid amounts are usually with a few tens of kWh of the daily numbers reported by sense.

comments.body:
@participant10 I think that is to be expected if you are using the "Daily" sensors. Here is why I think that:
* To present a consumption bar for a specific hour the panel needs to know the energy value at the start of that hour, and at the start of the next hour (so it can subtract)
* The daily sensor, while it has a last reset of midnight, has an "update" of something like 00:03 (or similar)
* And similarly the next update will be 01:03 (or similar), but almost never exactly on the hour
* So when the clock strikes 01:00 that second value needed is not there yet -> no bar
* When the clock strikes 02:00 there is a value from 00:03 and one from 01:03 so that 00:00 - 01:00 can be produced
* But, it is not 02:03 yet, so the value for the last hour cannot be computed yet.
* When the clock strikes 03:00 the 01:00 - 02:00 bar can finally be produced, etc.
* This seems consistent with this remark, somewhere on the configuration screen, that it "may take up to two hours" before changes in setup are reflected.

For me, it is currently 1:30AM and I do not see the 00:00 - 01:00 bar either. Not only that, but this:
![CleanShot 2022-02-06 at 01 45 19](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1332437/152675369-f3a042f6-f1ef-4723-b32b-da502a6e72a0.png)

If I am right above, I would expect that bar to possibly show up after 02:00 and not have to wait for 02:03.

Being right here also implies that, worst case scenario, the bars display up to an hour and 5 minutes late (because sense apparently only updates once an hour and is polled every 5 minutes). Best case will be 1 hr late.

I was still here at 02:02 and indeed the first bar appeared, while I confirmed the Daily sensor had last updated at 1:05. So the bar could appear before the second hour update came in (which did at 01:03, just after I looked). The circle panel now also reflects that first hour.
![CleanShot 2022-02-06 at 02 08 54](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1332437/152676088-3eb0495f-ba05-49b3-966c-1b485c48ac1e.png)
Daily updated at 01:05 and 02:05!

With my previously configured "integration" sensors the energy numbers get updated every 5 minutes and consequently, the 00:00 - 01:00 bar can appear anywhere between 01:00 and 01:05. This is clearly more dynamic and up to date behavior (and possibly desirable behavior), but the downside is that the errors introduced by the Riemann integral and undesirable effects of the chosen integration method (I use "left"), after accumulating for a day it is not as accurate as simply taking the daily value from the sense integration directly.

What I don't know (yet) is whether the trend data provided by the sensor api is simply not available until some time after the whole hour, or it would be available as soon as the hour passes, but the sense integration runs on a 5 minute schedule that might not coincide with the hour. I strongly suspect the latter, but need to experiment with the API to confirm or deny. If I would be right, then that strategy I mentioned earlier to change the update interval so that the next update happens as close to a multiple of 5 minutes as possible might help.

Altogether a different solution is to change (how I think) the energy panel itself works. Right now, I suspect it only looks at the relevant sensors once an hour because, after all, that's what's needed for the bars. If it could look more often, say every 5 minutes, the scenario above would pick up the first bar at or before 01:05. The values in the circle panel would still only update once an hour though, because reportedly sense totals only update once an hour.
